title: The Stag with One Eye
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A Stag, blind of one eye, was grazing close to the sea-shore and kept his sound eye turned towards the land, so as to be able to perceive the approach of the hounds, while the blind eye he turned towards the sea, never suspecting that any danger would threaten him from that quarter.

As it fell out, however, some sailors, coasting along the shore, spied him and shot an arrow at him, by which he was mortally wounded. As he lay dying, he said to himself, "Wretch that I am! I bethought me of the dangers of the land, whence none assailed me: but I feared no peril from the sea, yet thence has come my ruin."
Misfortune often assails us from an unexpected quarter.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, where is the Stag grazing?
options: Deep within a forest
On a distant hillside
Close to the sea-shore
Near a quiet farm

questions.prompt: According to the passage, which direction does the Stag keep his sound eye turned?
options: Towards the land
Towards the sea
Towards the sky
Towards the setting sun

questions.prompt: According to the passage, why does the Stag watch the land so carefully?
options: To find fresh grass to eat
To watch for other stags nearby
To see if the tide is coming in
To perceive the approach of the hounds

questions.prompt: According to the passage, who spies the Stag and shoots him?
options: A group of hunters on horseback
Some sailors coasting along the shore
Fishermen mending their nets
Villagers gathering shells

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Stag say as he lies dying?
options: That he never expected to be shot by an arrow at all
That he wished he had trusted the hounds more than the sailors
That he feared danger from the land but not the sea, yet the sea brought his ruin
That he regretted grazing so close to the shore

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Stag turn his blind eye toward the sea rather than the land?
options: He assumes danger could only come from the land, so he never expected a threat from the water
He cannot control which eye faces which direction
He wants to rest his sound eye by alternating its use
He is trying to watch for fish in the water

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what mistake does the Stag realize too late?
options: That hounds were actually more dangerous than sailors
That he should never have grazed near any shore
That his blindness in one eye was permanent
That danger can come from a direction one never expects

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "mortally wounded" mean?
options: Injured only slightly, with a quick recovery
Injured in a way that will cause death
Frightened but physically unharmed
Trapped but able to escape later

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "quarter" mean in "from that quarter"?
options: A sum of money
A period of time
A direction or side
A type of weapon

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable, given its closing line?
options: Misfortune can strike from a direction we never thought to guard against
Animals with a disability are always more vulnerable to hunters
The sea is more dangerous than the land for every creature
Sailors are more skilled hunters than those on land

questions.prompt: According to the passage, which of the Stag's eyes is blind?
options: The one turned toward the land
Both of his eyes
Neither; he can see fully from both
The one turned toward the sea

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what were the sailors doing when they spotted the Stag?
options: Fishing far out at sea
Coasting along the shore
Repairing their ship on the beach
Searching for fresh water

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what weapon do the sailors use against the Stag?
options: A spear
A net
An arrow
A sling and stone

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Stag call himself a "wretch" as he lies dying?
options: He recognizes that his own caution was misdirected the whole time
He believes the sailors cheated by using a weapon
He blames the hounds for driving him toward the sea
He regrets not fleeing sooner once he saw the ship

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the phrase "thence has come my ruin" tell us about where the fatal threat originated?
options: It came from the land, exactly where he expected danger
It came from another animal, not from a person at all
It came from a source he had never considered possible
It came from the sea, the very direction he considered safe

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "assails" mean in the closing line "assails us from an unexpected quarter"?
options: Comforts
Attacks
Warns
Follows

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A Stag is caught by hounds despite watching the land carefully
A Stag escapes both the land and sea dangers unharmed
A Stag guards against danger from the land but is fatally struck from the sea he trusted
A Stag loses sight in one eye after being attacked by sailors
